items.title: 15 things we've learned ahead of Gameweek 2 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Salah penalty claim strengthens Liverpool captaincy case for Gameweek 2
items.summary:
Mohamed Salah may now be Liverpool’s first-choice penalty taker, a development that further elevates his captaincy appeal for Gameweek 2. Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz remains a high-upside option but carries an early-substitution risk, while Arsenal’s attacking hierarchy looks clearer: Viktor Gyökeres receives no minutes in Gameweek 1 and Kai Havertz appears to be the first-choice No. 9.

At Manchester United, Amad Diallo’s injury makes Bryan Mbeumo’s minutes look much safer, improving his appeal as a secure attacking pick. Martin Ødegaard also shows signs of returning to his best, while Nico O’Reilly plays as Manchester City’s No. 10 but is not viewed as a reliable long-term option given City’s depth and rotation risk.

Several budget midfielders emerge as potential transfers. Mamadou Sangare posts two assists and 13 defensive-contribution points in only 75 minutes, suggesting he could offer the kind of value previously associated with Elliot Anderson. Maxim De Cuyper, priced at £4.5m as a defender, plays at left wing for Brighton, while Diego Gomez records an assist after 85 minutes at £5.0m. Angulo also returns in Gameweek 1 at the same price, although his pre-60-minute substitution is a warning over his security of minutes.

The forward market is also shifting. Ollie Watkins misses Aston Villa’s squad amid indications he could be sold, and Ismaïla Sarr is similarly absent from Crystal Palace’s squad, making both situations worth monitoring before committing transfers. Yoane Wissa impresses against Liverpool and joins the viable £6.0m-forward bracket, while Barry and Oli McBurnie offer cheaper £5.5m routes to fund premium midfielders. The main trade-off is clear: the cheaper forwards and midfielders create squad flexibility, but several come with uncertain roles, substitution risk or transfer speculation.
key_points: Mohamed Salah may be Liverpool’s penalty taker, making him an even stronger Gameweek 2 captaincy option.
Florian Wirtz offers attacking upside but is vulnerable to early substitutions.
Amad Diallo’s injury improves Bryan Mbeumo’s prospects of secure minutes at Manchester United.
Mamadou Sangare records two assists and 13 defensive-contribution points in 75 minutes and emerges as a budget-midfield watchlist option.
Brighton defender Maxim De Cuyper plays at left wing, giving the £4.5m pick major out-of-position upside.
Kai Havertz looks Arsenal’s first-choice striker after Viktor Gyökeres goes unused in Gameweek 1.
Ollie Watkins and Ismaïla Sarr miss their clubs’ squads, with potential sales creating immediate uncertainty.
Yoane Wissa, Barry and Oli McBurnie provide viable cheaper-forward alternatives, with Wissa especially impressive against Liverpool.

items.title: TOP 30K 🌎🚀 | FPL GENERAL'S TEAM REVEAL GW2 🔥 |  FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes captaincy holds firm as Haaland owners resist GW1 panic
items.summary:
A fast Gameweek 1 Bench Boost start changes little in the immediate plan. A 71-point return, including 16 points from the bench through Kinsky, Rodon, Leif Davis and the late punt on Slater, is treated as a success, especially with Erling Haaland blanking as captain and Bruno Fernandes also failing to return. The key message is patience: one game is too small a sample to rip up a squad built around early captaincy fixtures.

Bruno Fernandes remains the preferred Gameweek 2 captain at home to Ipswich, with Haaland vice-captain away to Crystal Palace. Manchester United disappoint badly at Hull, but the fixture process still stands: United have back-to-back promoted sides, and a home reaction at Old Trafford is expected. Luke Shaw’s one-pointer is not a sell yet either, with four chances created offering encouragement, although he may later make way for a stronger Defcon-style defender such as Ajer or Rodon.

The Gameweek 2 team is set up to roll the transfer. Kinsky starts in goal at home to Newcastle ahead of Verbruggen away to Chelsea, while Shaw, Ben White and Calafiori form the back three. Odegaard, Mbeumo, Szoboszlai and captain Bruno sit in midfield, with Haaland, Joao Pedro and Calvert-Lewin up front. Rodon is first bench at home to Brentford, with Slater ahead of Leif Davis because of his set-piece role. Calvert-Lewin is held for now, but Newcastle’s Wissa is the forward who most threatens that spot if his strong underlying numbers continue.

Early watchlists are forming rather than triggering immediate moves. De Cuyper’s huge Brighton haul is acknowledged, but his minutes remain a risk when Mitoma returns, while Pascal Gross looks more secure after lasting well and moving into advanced areas late on. Rutter at Brighton, McBurnie at Hull and Forest’s Eager Jesus are monitored among cheaper forwards, while Brobbey’s Sunderland appeal fades after their fixtures turn. The captaincy route remains Haaland in Gameweeks 3 and 5, a Chelsea asset such as Joao Pedro or Cole Palmer in Gameweek 4, and potentially Saka after a Gameweek 6 wildcard if Arsenal’s fixtures and form align.
key_points: The transfer is rolled in Gameweek 2, with no immediate injuries or structural problems forcing action.
Bruno Fernandes is the Gameweek 2 captain at home to Ipswich despite Manchester United’s poor opening display at Hull.
Erling Haaland stays central to the plan, with captaincy earmarked for Gameweeks 3 at home to Coventry and 5 at home to Sunderland.
Luke Shaw is a hold for Ipswich but is already pencilled in as a possible future sale for a better Defcon defender such as Ajer or Rodon.
Calvert-Lewin is not sold after one blank, but Wissa is the standout forward replacement to monitor after Newcastle impress in Gameweek 1.
De Cuyper’s explosive Brighton return is treated cautiously because Mitoma’s eventual comeback could threaten his starts.
Joao Pedro or Cole Palmer is the early Gameweek 4 captaincy route when Chelsea host Hull.
Managers on the Gameweek 2 Bench Boost plan are advised not to abandon it solely because Hull beat Manchester United in Gameweek 1.

items.title: FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW2 ✅
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes edges Haaland as Gameweek 2 captain while Arsenal defence rises
items.summary:
Gameweek 2 is framed as a week for patience rather than panic. Big Gameweek 1 hauls from players such as De Cuyper, Hinshelwood, Mendy and Aït-Nouri are treated with caution because last week’s points cannot be bought back and many of those returns are unlikely to repeat immediately. If a squad is structurally sound, rolling a transfer is still a sensible route, even though early wildcards can work in extreme cases.

David Raya again leads the goalkeeper projections after Arsenal allow only 0.2 xG and four shots in Gameweek 1, strengthening the case that double Arsenal defence could become a key setup. The drawback is price and squad-slot pressure: on a Gameweek 2 wildcard, a cheaper keeper such as Sanchez or Petrovic may be preferable to preserve Arsenal spots for Gabriel, a 4.5m defender punt and a midfielder like Ødegaard or Saka. In defence, Gabriel tops the projections, Virgil van Dijk remains attractive at home to Nottingham Forest, and mid-priced options such as Antonio Silva, Thiaw and the Leeds defenders are flagged for defensive-contribution potential and fixtures.

Bruno Fernandes is the standout Gameweek 2 captain call despite blanking in Gameweek 1, with the projections placing him ahead of Erling Haaland. Haaland is still the main forward option and has an inviting fixture against a Crystal Palace side weakened by departures and injury, but Bruno’s home fixture and role make him arguably the safest armband. Dominik Szoboszlai also rises in appeal at 7.0m after taking a Liverpool penalty and sharing set pieces, while Bukayo Saka is highlighted as a high-upside, low-owned route into Arsenal for managers who can afford him.

The main message on premium forwards and midfielders is to hold nerve. Alexander Isak blanks in a hostile return to Newcastle but posts 1.1 xGI and has Ipswich in Gameweek 3, so he should be kept. Matheus Cunha is another straightforward hold after a disappointing one-pointer, while Florian Wirtz gets a couple more weeks because of the upcoming Ipswich fixture. Among cheaper midfielders, Sangare, Anderson, Ndiaye, Hinshelwood and Gomez all enter the watchlist, with Sangare’s defensive contributions raising his floor even if the attacking returns slow.

The no-Haaland structure remains viable because the money can be spread into combinations such as Isak, Palmer and Saka, but the risk is obvious: Haaland can punish non-owners with a haul at any time. The best projected Gameweek 2 squad even omits him, showing how competitive the alternatives are, but captaincy and team structure should be judged on repeatable roles, fixtures and minutes rather than one volatile opening round.
key_points: Bruno Fernandes is projected above Erling Haaland for Gameweek 2 captaincy and remains a strong pick despite his opening blank.
Rolling a free transfer is sensible for many teams, with the warning not to chase isolated Gameweek 1 hauls from defenders and cheap midfielders.
David Raya is the top goalkeeper projection, but wildcarders may prefer Sanchez or Petrovic to keep Arsenal slots open for outfield players.
Gabriel leads the defender projections, while Van Dijk at home to Nottingham Forest and 5.0m options such as Antonio Silva and Thiaw are notable alternatives.
Bukayo Saka is highlighted as a major upside pick at only around 10% ownership, though fitting him alongside Haaland and Bruno is difficult.
Dominik Szoboszlai looks a strong 7.0m option if he keeps penalties and set pieces for Liverpool.
Alexander Isak is a hold after strong underlying numbers and an Ipswich fixture in Gameweek 3, despite blanking at Newcastle.
Sangare, Anderson, Ndiaye, Hinshelwood and Gomez are the cheaper midfielders to monitor, with Gomez preferred among the 5.0m bracket.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 2 Early Thoughts 🔥 Szoboszlai essential? 🤔 Sell Wirtz? ❌
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes gets Ipswich captaincy nod as Gameweek 2 patience takes priority
items.summary:
Gameweek 2 is framed as a week for restraint: roll the free transfer wherever possible and take two moves into Gameweek 3. The logic is that Gameweek 1 squads are effectively wildcard-built for the opening fixtures, and one set of blanks is not enough evidence to rip up those plans. Exceptions exist, particularly if a non-playing pick such as Ismaila Sarr is at risk of leaving Crystal Palace and there is no bench cover, but the default move is to avoid early transfers, protect flexibility and reduce the need for hits later.

Manchester United assets are firm holds despite a poor 2-0 defeat to Hull. Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw all have Ipswich at home in Gameweek 2, a fixture strong enough to override one bad performance. Mbeumo’s underlying numbers are encouraging, with 0.5 xG and 0.23 xA, and Amad’s possible six-week absence should help his minutes, even if he is not playing as a No 9. Fernandes remains a viable captaincy option for Ipswich at home, even if premium alternatives impress elsewhere.

Liverpool’s situation is more nuanced. Florian Wirtz is a hold despite an early 62-minute substitution, with Forest at home in Gameweek 2 and Ipswich away in Gameweek 3 still too good to sell before gaining more information. Dominik Szoboszlai looks increasingly attractive after taking a high-pressure late penalty against Newcastle; at £7.0m, penalties, set pieces and a No 8 role with box threat make him outstanding value. Even so, chasing him immediately from Wirtz is not advised, particularly just to avoid price changes. Ekitike/Isak is also a hold for the next two fixtures, though his appeal drops if he is not Liverpool’s main penalty taker.

Mamadou Sangare emerges as a standout Brentford watchlist pick after 13 defensive contributions and two assists in 75 minutes against Spurs. At £5.5m he profiles like a possible Elliot Anderson-style value midfielder, combining DefCon points with some attacking output, and he is a strong replacement for Sarr if a transfer is necessary. Elsewhere, Brighton’s De Cuyper is intriguing after playing left wing as a £4.5m defender, but Chelsea away and future minutes risk temper the excitement; Hinshelwood’s brace is appealing but early substitutions remain a concern. Erling Haaland owners simply hold through Palace away, while non-owners likely need a plan to buy him for Coventry at home in Gameweek 3, where he is viewed as the clear best captain.

The current Gameweek 2 squad plan is to roll the transfer and captain Bruno Fernandes against Ipswich. Raya and Calafiori face Aston Villa away, with Ballard against Fulham and Maguire against Ipswich completing the defence. Fernandes, Mbeumo, Szoboszlai and Semenyo start in midfield, with Ekitike, João Pedro and Calvert-Lewin up front. The main dilemma is benching Zolis away to Villa despite his strong Gameweek 1, with Semenyo the only realistic alternative to drop; De Cuyper and Nico Williams stay benched because their fixtures are Chelsea away and Liverpool away.
key_points: Roll the Gameweek 2 transfer if possible, with two free transfers in Gameweek 3 seen as far more valuable than reacting to one week of data.
Bruno Fernandes is the preferred Gameweek 2 captain in the sample squad because Manchester United face Ipswich at home.
Manchester United assets such as Fernandes, Mbeumo, Maguire and Shaw are holds despite the opening defeat, as Ipswich at home remains a prime fixture.
Dominik Szoboszlai looks excellent value at £7.0m if he is Liverpool’s first-choice penalty taker, but selling Florian Wirtz for him immediately is not recommended.
Mamadou Sangare is a strong £5.5m watchlist pick and a sensible Ismaila Sarr replacement if Sarr is unavailable or sold.
Erling Haaland is a hold for owners and a priority buy for non-owners ahead of Coventry at home in Gameweek 3, where he is the standout captain.
Phil Foden is a hold for Palace away despite long-term Manchester City minutes concerns, while Rayan Cherki is only a watchlist option for now.
Zolis versus Semenyo is the main benching dilemma, with Zolis likely benched away to Aston Villa despite his strong Gameweek 1.

items.title: GW1 Is Over... Here's What I'm Doing for GW2
items.headline: Haaland moves ahead of Bruno for Gameweek 2 captaincy as Bench Boost plan survives
items.summary:
Gameweek 1 produces enough shocks to make patience the main FPL message. Manchester United’s defeat at Hull is the biggest xG mismatch of the week, with Hull scoring twice from set pieces despite offering almost nothing in open play, while United look disjointed rather than devoid of individual FPL promise. Bryan Mbeumo is the clearest positive: four shots, 0.50 xG, 0.23 xA, right-sided corners and strong minutes security with Amad out for several weeks. Bruno Fernandes is more disappointing, taking lower-quality shots, but United still top the Gameweek 2 goal projections at home to Ipswich.

The early captaincy lean shifts towards Erling Haaland for Manchester City’s trip to Crystal Palace. City are not fully convincing defensively against Bournemouth, but their attack creates enough for Haaland to have scored more than once, and their Gameweek 2 projection sits close to United’s. Bruno remains a viable captain for non-Haaland squads, with En-Nesyri mentioned as a punt, but Haaland’s chances, City’s result and United’s attacking mess make him the preferred early choice.

Arsenal’s 3-0 win over Coventry confirms the appeal of their assets without creating an automatic transfer rush. Bukayo Saka returns with a goal, Ben White looks creative from right-back, and Riccardo Calafiori repeatedly takes up dangerous inside and advanced positions. Kristoffer Salvesen is especially busy, producing five shots and three key passes, but buyers are warned to wait on Arsenal’s transfer business after the exits of Trossard and Martinelli, because a new left winger could threaten his role. Coventry should not be judged harshly for losing away to Arsenal; Bobby Thomas still looks a strong defensive-contribution option, and Milan van Ewijk retains attacking routes to points.

The planned Gameweek 2 Bench Boost remains on. Coventry’s home match against Hull still has appeal despite reduced clean-sheet odds, because Hull’s threat against United is almost entirely set-piece based and Coventry were one of the Championship’s best teams at defending set plays last season. Thomas can score through defensive contributions or set-piece threat, Van Ewijk offers attacking upside, and Rushworth has clean-sheet and save-point potential. With no obvious must-buy emerging from Gameweek 1, the recommended approach is to avoid rash transfers unless dealing with injuries such as Ferdi Kadioglu, while also monitoring Elliot Anderson’s niggle and Chelsea’s Monday performance before final decisions.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the early preferred Gameweek 2 captain over Bruno Fernandes because City create good chances and United look chaotic despite strong projections against Ipswich.
Bryan Mbeumo is the best Manchester United hold after Gameweek 1, combining shots, chance creation, corners and improved minutes security while Amad is out.
The Gameweek 2 Bench Boost plan stays alive, especially for Coventry assets at home to Hull, with Bobby Thomas and Milan van Ewijk offering routes beyond a clean sheet.
Do not rush into Kristoffer Salvesen despite excellent underlying numbers until Arsenal’s potential new left-wing signing situation is clearer.
Brighton assets impress against a weakened Aston Villa, with Maxim De Cuyper playing effectively as a left winger, but European minutes need monitoring before Gameweek 2.
Brentford’s win over Spurs boosts interest in Sangare and Kristoffer Ajer, while Igor Thiago’s missed penalty is a concern for those relying on spot-kick value.
Szoboszlai taking Liverpool’s penalty ahead of Isak is encouraging for owners, but it is not treated as proof he has penalties permanently.
Transfers should generally be rolled unless injuries force action, with Ferdi Kadioglu flagged as injured and Elliot Anderson needing monitoring.

items.title: My FPL GW2 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 2 TEAM 🎯
items.headline: Hold Bruno for Ipswich as Haaland dilemma looms in Gameweek 3
items.summary:
Gameweek 1 produces plenty of noise, but the immediate message is not to overreact. Arsenal assets start strongly in a 3-0 win, with Zolis directly involved in seven shots and credited with an FPL assist, while Ødegaard again looks underpriced at £6.5m if he can stay fit. Saka going straight into the Arsenal XI is another positive, and Arsenal also lead the clean-sheet projections over the next five gameweeks, though White and Calafiori may become rotation headaches longer term.

Manchester United are the main concern after a flat defeat to newly promoted Hull, but their Gameweek 2 home fixture against Ipswich is the reason to hold rather than panic sell. Bruno Fernandes remains firmly in the Gameweek 2 conversation despite blanking, especially for managers who backed him as captain in Gameweek 1. Haaland also blanks for the first time in an opening gameweek, but he still records four shots in the box, and Manchester City sit top for projected goals over the next five. Their Gameweek 3 home match against Coventry is the major decision point for no-Haaland teams, with many likely to consider a Free Hit, Wildcard or another aggressive route to cover him.

The current squad is set up in a 3-4-3 for Gameweek 2: Kinsky; Calafiori, Maguire and White; Mbeumo, Bruno, Szoboszlai and Zolis; Brobbey, Haaland and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. The bench is Verbruggen, Hume, Gross and Dorgu, with Hume available to step in if midweek injuries hit. With 12 teams playing before the deadline, including Brighton in Europe and several sides in the League Cup, the plan is to avoid an early transfer and roll, moving to three free transfers for Gameweek 3.

Transfer strategy is shaped by an intended Wildcard around Gameweek 4. The next decision is whether to use a move in Gameweek 3 to attack Manchester City at home to Coventry or Liverpool against Ipswich, or bank again and try to build towards five free transfers after the Wildcard. Longer term, Chelsea’s Gameweek 4 home match against Hull and Manchester United’s tough fixture away to Manchester City are part of the appeal of an early reset. Szoboszlai also emerges as an important watch after taking and scoring Liverpool’s late penalty at Newcastle, suggesting he may have penalties in addition to set pieces.
key_points: Do not panic sell Manchester United assets after one poor match, with Ipswich at home in Gameweek 2 still a strong fixture for Bruno Fernandes and Maguire owners.
Haaland blanks in Gameweek 1 but Manchester City lead the five-gameweek goal projections, making their Gameweek 3 home match against Coventry a key problem for no-Haaland teams.
The Gameweek 2 team is set to roll a transfer with Kinsky, Calafiori, Maguire, White, Mbeumo, Bruno, Szoboszlai, Zolis, Brobbey, Haaland and Calvert-Lewin starting.
Captaincy is framed around whether to stick with Bruno after the Gameweek 1 blank or move to another premium such as Haaland, rather than making a reactionary squad sale.
Arsenal assets look strong after the 3-0 opener, with Zolis heavily involved, Saka starting, Ødegaard appealing at £6.5m and Arsenal top for projected clean sheets.
Szoboszlai’s penalty for Liverpool is a major FPL note, as he may now combine penalties, free-kicks, corners and bonus potential.
A planned Gameweek 4 Wildcard remains attractive because Chelsea get Hull at home while Manchester United face Manchester City.
No early transfer is planned because 12 teams play midweek, and Hume can cover from the bench if injuries or rotation news emerges.

items.title: MY FPL GW2 TRANSFER PLANS! 📝 More Arsenal or Buy Sangare? 🤔 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Bruno keeps armband despite United flop as Arsenal and Sangaré tempt early transfers
items.summary:
Gameweek 1 delivers the usual FPL shock: Bruno Fernandes and Erling Haaland both blank, while cheaper picks such as Doucouré and Sangaré haul. The early Bench Boost pays off with more than 20 points from Verbruggen, Gomez, Ajer and Diop, and the Gameweek 2 squad is strong enough to avoid a panic move. Kulusevski is held despite disappointment at Brentford, with Spurs now facing Newcastle at home and owning three home matches in the next four between Gameweeks 2 and 6.

Arsenal are the obvious temptation after a convincing 3-0 opening win and Aston Villa’s poor display against Brighton. Their Gameweek 2 trip to Villa, followed by Chelsea at home and Sunderland away, makes a double or triple-up attractive. The preference remains a defensive double-up long term, with Saliba, Ben White and Calafiori all appealing, while Ødegaard and Saka also post strong involvement numbers. If a transfer is made this week, it is most likely for an Arsenal player, with Saliba and Ødegaard the leading targets.

The stronger recommendation, though, is to roll the Gameweek 2 transfer unless there is a genuine problem. One free transfer is inflexible, and one week of data is not enough to justify sideways moves such as Mbeumo to Ødegaard or Maguire to Ben White. Saving transfers creates more flexibility for the fixture swings ahead, especially with Manchester City hosting Coventry in Gameweek 3 and Chelsea getting Hull at home soon after. Price changes are also not yet forcing action: Calafiori and Trippier look close to rises, Martinelli is a possible faller, and Sangaré is not expected to rise immediately.

Haaland is an easy hold for owners despite blanking at home to Bournemouth, with Crystal Palace away still a decent fixture and Coventry at home in Gameweek 3 a major reason not to sell. Non-owners can stay committed to their structure for now because the Haaland decision was never just a one-week call. Manchester United assets are also held despite a poor 2-0 opening defeat: Bruno, Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire all have Ipswich at home, and Mbeumo in particular looks one of United’s brighter attackers. Bruno remains the current captain over Haaland, mainly because he is at home, though neither player’s Gameweek 1 performance inspires full confidence.

Sangaré is the standout cheap midfielder after hitting defensive-contribution points in just 75 minutes and adding two assists for Brentford. His set-piece involvement and role around the edge of the box make him look more than a passive DEFCON pick, and he may become a set-and-forget 5.5m midfielder. He is the priority buy for anyone who must make a cheap midfield transfer, but there is no need to rip up a good squad to get him before Gameweek 2.
key_points: The preferred Gameweek 2 move is no move: rolling the free transfer is favoured unless injuries or major issues appear.
Bruno Fernandes currently keeps the captaincy for Ipswich at home, narrowly ahead of Erling Haaland away to Crystal Palace.
Haaland owners should hold through Palace away and Coventry at home in Gameweek 3, while non-owners can stick with their original structure.
Arsenal are the main transfer target if acting early, with Saliba and Ødegaard highlighted and a defensive double-up still preferred long term.
Manchester United assets Bruno, Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire are holds for Ipswich at home despite a poor opening performance.
Sangaré looks the best midfielder at 6.0m or under after strong DEFCON potential, set-piece involvement and two assists, but he is not an urgent Gameweek 2 buy.
Calafiori and Trippier are close to early price rises, Martinelli is a possible faller, and Sangaré is not yet expected to rise quickly.

items.title: FPL LIVE RANK! What You Need To Know 📊
items.headline: FPL.page and FPL Focal launch live rank tool using official FPL data
items.summary:
FPL managers can now track their live overall rank through FPL.page and the FPL Focal app, with the tool pulling directly from the official Fantasy Premier League feed for full rank accuracy.

The live rank feature factors in key in-game updates including live bonus points, auto substitutions and defensive contribution points, giving managers a more complete picture of their gameweek position before the official update.

To use it, managers only need their FPL ID. This can be found on the FPL website by opening the Points page and copying the number shown in the page URL. Entering that ID at FPL.page/rank or in the FPL Focal app returns the live rank instantly.
key_points: Live rank is available at FPL.page/rank and in the FPL Focal app.

Managers only need their FPL ID to use the feature.
The FPL ID is the number in the URL on the Points page of the FPL website.
The tool is used by more than half a million FPL managers.

items.title: FPL GW1 LIVE DEADLINE STREAM 📸 | LOCKING IN FOR THE NEW SEASON! 🚀 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes takes Gameweek 1 armband as Szoboszlai shapes an early Bench Boost squad
items.summary:
The Gameweek 1 squad locks in with the Bench Boost active and Bruno Fernandes captained for Manchester United’s trip to Hull. Erling Haaland stays in the team despite not taking the armband in either of the first two gameweeks, because he is likely to be needed as captain in Gameweeks 3 and 5 and selling him would force awkward transfers or an early chip. Bruno gets the nod because Hull and Ipswich in the opening two fixtures make him feel the safest captaincy route, even if Haaland’s ownership and Gameweek 1 record remain a clear risk.

Dominik Szoboszlai is the key late structural call. He comes into midfield alongside Bryan Mbeumo, Bruno and Solace, with the appeal built on Liverpool’s strong opening five fixtures and Szoboszlai’s security for 90-minute starts. Wirtz is viewed as having more upside, but Szoboszlai is preferred as the safer longer-term Liverpool route. The compromise is a lighter defence and a cheaper eighth attacker, with Brighton’s Gomez taking the final midfield slot despite being identified as the weakest pick.

The Bench Boost is built around Kinsky, Calafiori, Maguire, Rodon, Ajer, Dop, Verbruggen and Gomez, with the front line of Haaland, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and João Pedro unchanged throughout pre-season. Verbruggen, Ajer, Dop and Gomez are the boost players, all expected to start and all with playable home fixtures or Defcon routes. The target is modest: a double-digit Bench Boost is acceptable, with one clean sheet, one attacking return or a couple of Defcon scores likely enough to make the chip worthwhile.

There is heavy awareness of the trade-offs. Rodon is selected over Muharemovic because the money is needed elsewhere, even though Muharemovic has the better Defcon profile. Maguire is preferred to Shaw for greater set-piece threat and some Defcon potential, especially with Casemiro absent. Ajer is treated as a 5.0-style Defcon defender at 4.5, while Gomez is kept over Slater or Nottingham Forest’s Sangare because he has more attacking upside and useful Gameweek 3-4 fixtures against Leeds and Coventry. The plan is to roll transfers early, possibly move Mbeumo around Gameweeks 3-4, and Wildcard around Gameweek 6 unless the team can be stretched longer.
key_points: Bench Boost is active in Gameweek 1, with Wildcard 6 the current plan and no transfer planned for Gameweek 2.
Bruno Fernandes is captain over Haaland for Hull away; Haaland stays because he is wanted for captaincy in Gameweeks 3 and 5.
Dominik Szoboszlai is preferred to Wirtz for Liverpool coverage because of minutes security and strong opening fixtures.
Final squad structure is light in defence: Kinsky, Calafiori, Maguire and Rodon start, with Verbruggen, Ajer, Dop and Gomez forming the Bench Boost bench.
Gomez is the main uncertain spot, but he is kept over Slater or Sangare because Brighton’s injuries and fixtures give him short-term upside.
Rodon is chosen over Muharemovic mainly for budget reasons, despite Muharemovic’s stronger Defcon appeal.
Maguire is preferred to Shaw due to set-piece goal threat and possible Defcon points.
Cole Palmer is avoided because of price, better value in João Pedro/Rogers-type picks, and uncertainty over Chelsea penalties.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 1 Deadline Stream 🚀 588th last season 👀 Fernandes (c) 🤔
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes gets the armband as Haaland is sold for an aggressive Gameweek 1 bench boost
items.summary:
The Gameweek 1 plan lands on the aggressive side: Bench Boost is active immediately, Bruno Fernandes is captain, and Erling Haaland is left out despite Manchester City hosting Bournemouth. The logic is that if Haaland is not being captained, his £14m-plus price can be spread across a stronger 15-man squad for the opening bench boost. It is a high-risk call because Haaland is expected to start and score, but the bet is that Bruno, plus the upgraded players around the squad, can match or beat him over the opening weeks.

The final structure is a no-Haaland bench-boost squad built around David Raya in goal, Arsenal defensive cover through Riccardo Calafiori rather than Gabriel, Harry Maguire, Ballard, Nico Williams and the short-term De Cuyper punt. In midfield, Bruno Fernandes is locked as captain, with attacking upside also coming from Antoine Semenyo and Zolis after a late switch away from a safer Ben White/Ndiaye combination. Alexander Isak and Joao Pedro are key forward picks, with Isak effectively asked to cover the Haaland omission before a likely reset.

The whole approach points strongly towards an early Wildcard, most likely in Gameweek 3. That allows an immediate move back to Haaland for Manchester City’s fixture swing, alongside possible City additions such as Nico O’Reilly or Phil Foden if minutes look secure. The alternative Haaland draft is acknowledged as safer and more “classic FPL”, with a cheaper bench of players such as Gomez and O’Shea, but it offers less upside for Bench Boost and still probably leads to an early Wildcard because of Chelsea, Arsenal and City fixture swings.

The main risks are obvious: Arsenal could lose the clean sheet, Bruno could blank as captain, and Haaland could punish the fade with a brace or hat-trick against Bournemouth. There are also minutes doubts around Calafiori, De Cuyper and some of the mid-price punts. But the call is deliberately made now: attack Gameweek 1 with 15 players, roll in Gameweek 2 if possible, then Wildcard in Gameweek 3 to rebuild around Haaland, City and Chelsea information.
key_points: Bench Boost is active in Gameweek 1 to exploit a strong 15-man squad and avoid saving the chip for uncertain future doubles.
Bruno Fernandes is captain ahead of Haaland, with penalties and security making him the preferred armband despite Haaland’s Bournemouth fixture.
Erling Haaland is omitted in the final draft; the plan is to bring him back on a Gameweek 3 Wildcard unless circumstances change.
David Raya is retained as the Arsenal defensive anchor, with Calafiori selected but Gabriel ultimately missed in the final no-Haaland structure.
Late move: Zolis and Nico Williams come in over the safer Ben White/Ndiaye combination, increasing upside but adding regret risk.
Semenyo is valued for the early fixture run and especially Gameweek 3, while Isak is trusted as the premium forward placeholder before the Wildcard.
De Cuyper is treated as a short-term Bench Boost punt who needs an early Wildcard to manage minutes and fixture risk.
Gameweek 3 Wildcard targets include Haaland, possible Manchester City assets such as O’Reilly or Foden, and Chelsea players from Gameweek 4.

Liverpool are missing Ekitike, Bradley, Leon and Joe Gomez, but Isak and Gakpo are expected to start.
